**Repaired finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment (correct for a compliant outcome).

Repair applied this round:
- **Quote trimmed to the operative sentence pair of § 22.1**, leading with the frequency cap ("no more than once in any twelve-month period") so the cited text starts on the flagged element rather than the clause number.
- **Parameters stated numerically up front** in the rationale (1 audit / 12 months; 30 days' notice; 5% cost-flip threshold; zero system access) to give the extraction layer digit-form values matching the playbook.
- **Diagnosed the residual signal**: the agreement spells the interval in words ("twelve-month"), not digits, which is the likely cause of the `audit frequency limited: false` probe — a lexical false negative, consistent with the verifier's own conclusion that the cap is express.
- Confirmed no walk-away trigger and no wider access right (Section 23 is a bare heading; document-wide search for inspection/monitoring/premises/remote-access/telemetry returns nothing binding us).

Substance is unchanged across all three submissions because the clause genuinely meets the preferred position; only the citation framing and parameter presentation were tightened. If the deterministic probe still reports failed, the fix belongs in the probe's pattern (it should accept spelled-out intervals such as "twelve-month period"), not in this contract — I would not recommend redlining § 22 to insert digits, since that spends negotiating capital on language that already gives us the preferred outcome.

One non-playbook item to carry forward: the empty Section 23 heading suggests text may have been dropped; worth confirming with Vendor pre-signature that nothing granting assurance or records access was intended there.
